nieuw.titel: Use 3D6 random movement to catch shooting units
nieuw.tekst: Use units with 3D6 random movement to threaten shooting units that rely on charge reactions. The speaker says these targets must hold instead of standing and shooting or firing and fleeing.
nieuw.waarom: He says most shooting units are lightly armoured, hit back weakly and try to avoid combat, so 3D6 random movers can decimate them.

bronnen.citaat: As I mentioned, it counters shooting armies.

nieuw.titel: Use random movement to deny cavalry their countercharge
nieuw.tekst: Threaten countercharge-dependent cavalry with 3D6 random movement. The speaker says contact forces them to hold, removing the countercharge safety net that can encourage aggressive movement.
nieuw.waarom: He says heavy cavalry benefits significantly from countercharge and can move more aggressively when it expects to use it.
nieuw.voorbeeld: His opponent left a ten-inch gap between knights and his Mangler Squigs. He rolled twelve, reached the knights without allowing a countercharge, and inflicted heavy casualties before they broke and fled.
nieuw.wanneerNiet: He describes the Mangler Squigs' damage rolls in this example as unusually high.

bronnen.citaat: They also, as I mentioned, threaten countercharge units and armies that rely on that.

nieuw.titel: Use 3D6 variance to pressure enemy movement
nieuw.tekst: Use the possibility of a high 3D6 movement roll to put pressure on enemy positioning. The speaker recommends exploiting this variance: opponents may underestimate it or play too defensively around it.
nieuw.waarom: He says the high potential threat range forces opponents to respect the unit, sometimes more than they need to.
nieuw.voorbeeld: His Hell Pit Abomination's advance made Alex hide a unit behind a forest and move another unit back. A subsequent high movement roll still let the monster reach its preferred target, and Alex committed more resources to containing it.
nieuw.wanneerNiet: He says an eighteen-inch roll is difficult and the fourteen- or fifteen-inch roll in his example will not happen every time.

bronnen.citaat: more people should be utilizing the variance of it

extraCitaten.citaat: your opponent has to respect it
often they go a little too far in the other direction

nieuw.titel: Consider unseen targets when moving randomly
nieuw.tekst: In the speaker's interpretation, random movement lets you attack a preferred target even without line of sight. Consider this when an enemy shelters behind terrain; he is fairly confident in this interpretation but invites correction.
nieuw.waarom: He reasons that the unit does not declare a charge and that the charge movement restrictions he cites do not require line of sight.
nieuw.voorbeeld: His Hell Pit Abomination moved through a forest into his preferred target, which it could not see. He hoped to break through into the combat involving his surrounded Stormvermin.
nieuw.wanneerNiet: He says the move must still obey charge movement restrictions, including the shortest route and alignment. He also says you cannot move out of one target arc into another before making contact.

bronnen.citaat: you do not need to be able to see your opponent

nieuw.tekst: He considers the Hell Pit Abomination playable because its 3D6 movement makes it a utility piece. Use that unpredictability rather than treating it only as a large monster that chases targets.

nieuw.tekst: He considers Mangler Squigs the ideal random-movement unit. Take them for their potential to change the game dramatically at a low points cost.
nieuw.waarom: He says that at 95 points their ability to alter the game state is probably unmatched at that price.
